role: Son of Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) and Fatima (RA)
summary: Hasan ibn Ali (RA) was the eldest grandson of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through Fatima (RA) and Ali (RA). He succeeded his father Ali as Caliph in 40 AH but abdicated in favor of Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan within six months, fulfilling the Prophet's ﷺ prophecy that he would reconcile two large groups of Muslims. He is recognized as the fifth of the Rightly Guided Caliphs by many classical scholars and is held in the highest esteem in Sunni tradition as a member of the Ahl al-Bayt.
biography:
Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Hashimi al-Qurashi was born in Madinah in 3 AH (approximately 624 CE), the first son of Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) and Fatima bint Muhammad (RA). When news of his birth reached the Prophet ﷺ, he came to the household, called the adhan in the newborn's right ear, the iqamah in the left ear, named him Hasan, and performed the aqiqah for him. These practices, recorded in the Sunan of al-Tirmidhi and Sunan Abi Dawud, became the normative Sunnah for newborns.

The Prophet ﷺ's affection for Hasan was famous and openly expressed. He would frequently carry Hasan on his shoulder during prayer, placing him down for prostration and picking him up again when he rose. Ibn Sa'd records in al-Tabaqat al-Kubra (Vol. 3) that the Prophet ﷺ would say: 'O Allah, I love him; love those who love him.' Perhaps the most consequential praise was the prophecy recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Fitan): 'This son of mine is a Sayyid (leader), and perhaps Allah will bring peace between two large groups of Muslims through him.' This prophecy, narrated by Abu Bakra (RA), shaped Islamic historical understanding of Hasan's caliphate.

Hasan grew up in the Prophet's household and was thus counted among the Sahaba — he personally saw, heard, and was in the company of the Prophet ﷺ. He narrated hadith directly from his grandfather, his mother Fatima, his father Ali, and other companions. Al-Dhahabi in Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' (Vol. 3) notes that while his hadith narrations were relatively few — given that he was a child when the Prophet died — his stature as a companion is beyond question.

Hasan was also one of the five people wrapped in the Prophet's cloak in the hadith al-kisa' (Event of the Cloak), and is named in the Quranic verse of Mubahala (Quran 3:61) as among the 'children' (abna'ana) whom the Prophet brought to the challenge against the Christians of Najran. Classical Sunni exegetes including al-Tabari, Ibn Kathir, and al-Qurtubi identify Hasan and Husayn as the 'children' referenced in this verse.

During the caliphate of Uthman (RA), Hasan participated in several military campaigns. When Ali (RA) became caliph in 35 AH, Hasan stood alongside his father through the turbulent period that followed. He fought at the Battle of the Camel and the Battle of Siffin with his father, though he and Husayn reportedly counseled de-escalation at several points. When Ali (RA) was assassinated in Kufah in 40 AH, the people of Kufah gave bay'ah (oath of allegiance) to Hasan as Caliph.

Hasan's caliphate lasted approximately six or seven months. Faced with the military strength of Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan's forces in Syria and, critically, aware of the divisions and unreliability of his own troops in Kufah, Hasan chose to negotiate peace rather than press a civil war that would have cost thousands of Muslim lives. He abdicated the caliphate to Muawiyah in 41 AH on conditions that included just treatment of his supporters and the restoration of rights to Ali's followers. Classical historians including al-Tabari record these negotiations in detail. This act is understood in Sunni tradition as a manifestation of wisdom, generosity, and the prioritization of Muslim unity over personal authority — fulfilling the prophetic hadith word for word. The year 41 AH became known as 'Am al-Jama'ah (the Year of the Congregation/Unity).

After his abdication, Hasan retired to Madinah and devoted his remaining years to scholarship, worship, and family. He died in Madinah in 50 AH (approximately 670 CE), according to the most accepted report. The cause of his death is recorded by Ibn Sa'd and al-Dhahabi as an illness; some narrations indicate he was poisoned. Al-Dhahabi records the accounts without drawing firm conclusions about their reliability, and classical Sunni scholars have generally treated the question of the manner of his death with scholarly caution. Husayn wished to bury him next to the Prophet ﷺ, but this was prevented after a dispute, and Hasan was buried in the Baqi' cemetery in Madinah. Usamah ibn Zayd (RA) and other companions were present at his burial.

Hasan ibn Ali (RA) is regarded in classical Sunni scholarship as the fifth of the Rightly Guided Caliphs by many scholars, including Ibn Kathir who counts him in al-Bidayah wal-Nihayah. Al-Dhahabi places him among the greatest members of the Ahl al-Bayt in piety and character. His title 'Sayyid Shabab Ahl al-Jannah' (Leader of the Youth of Paradise) derives directly from the authenticated prophetic hadith in Sunan al-Tirmidhi and Sunan Ibn Majah.

key_events.event: Born in Madinah; Prophet ﷺ called adhan, named him Hasan, and performed aqiqah
Named in connection with the verse of Mubahala (Quran 3:61) — the challenge to the Christians of Najran
Death of the Prophet ﷺ — Hasan was approximately 7-8 years old
Fought alongside his father Ali (RA) at the Battle of the Camel and Battle of Siffin
Became Caliph after the assassination of his father Ali (RA)
Abdicated caliphate to Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan — 'Am al-Jama'ah (Year of Unity)
Died in Madinah; buried in al-Baqi' cemetery

notable_traits: Closest physical resemblance to the Prophet ﷺ among all people, per multiple narrations
Extraordinary generosity — narrated to have divided his wealth with the poor multiple times during his life
Prioritized Muslim unity over personal political authority by abdicating the caliphate
Fulfillment of the prophetic prophecy of reconciling two large Muslim factions
Deep piety and love for the Quran

key_relationships.father: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) — fourth Caliph
key_relationships.mother: Fatima al-Zahra (RA) — daughter of the Prophet ﷺ
